newsitem.title: INDIA: India Hindujas to invest $3 bln in infrastructure.
newsitem.headline: India Hindujas to invest $3 bln in infrastructure.

text.p: India's Hinduja Group plans to invest up to $3 billion in the country's infrastructure sector over the next few months, a top group official said on Friday.

"The Hinduja group plans an investment of $6 billion in various projects in India mainly in infrastructure," A. F. Couto, special director of the investment group's flagship company Ashok Leyland Ltd, told a seminar in Bombay.
"We have already invested about $3 billion, and expect to invest another three billion soon," Couto told Reuters later.
But he said the time-frame of the investment would depend on the pace of regulatory procedures and government clearances.

India has opened many sectors of industry to private enterprise since it began tearing down the walls of a socialist command economy in 1991. But its crumbling infrastructure threatens to slow the pace of further reform.

To meet the growing demand for power, about 240 billion rupees will have to be invested annually over the next 15 years, experts estimate. About 400 billion rupees will have to be invested in the telecommunications sector by the year 2010.
The bulk of these funds will have to come from private enterprise, some domestically, but much from foreign investors.

Couto said the Hinduja Group planned to direct funds in eight areas -- banking and finance, information technology, media and communications, property development, chemicals, agribusiness, trading and merchandising, transport, oil and power and project development.
"The group has positioned itself strategically to seize the emerging opportunities in the aftermath of globalisation," Couto added.
"About $3 billion has already been put into our power project at Vishakapatnam, the tie-up between the Hinduja group and Lufthansa, and into cable television," he said.

The projects include a 1,000 megawatt coal-based power project in the southern state of Andhra Pradesh, an air cargo joint venture with German airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG, and the IN Cable television network, with a subscriber base of two million.
The Hinduja group is also part of a consortium to develop a new international airport at Bombay.
Couto said the group will bid for some of the 50 different infrastructure projects which the government of the western state of Maharashtra plans to begin offering to private investors in February.
The total value of these projects is placed at $5 billion, government officials said.
The group also plans to build superhighways in the neighbouring tourist resort state of Goa.

Last month, the Hinduja Group announced it would take a 51 percent stake in a $1.1 billion oil refinery in India's eastern state of Orissa, along with Bechtel Group Inc of the U.S. and Japan's Sumitomo Corp, the Economic Times newspaper reported.
Last December, Ashok Leyland Ltd opened a $176 million state-of-the-art plant to manufacture heavy commercial vehicles at Hosur in the southern state of Tamil Nadu.
It will produce trucks for the domestic market, as well as potentially catering to European, Asian and African markets.

Ashok Leyland's net profit for the six months ended September 30, 1996, rose to 571 million rupees from 485 million in the corresponding period last year. Net sales climbed to 11.52 billion rupees from 8.28 billion rupees.
